subject: social-studies
title: Water Supply: From Rain to Tap, Stage by Stage

slides.heading: Water Supply: From Rain to Tap, Stage by Stage
bullets: How Singapore gets clean water: rain is collected in a reservoir as raw water, the raw water is drawn to the treatment works, treatment stages remove dirt and germs step by step so the cleanliness bar climbs, and only the cleaned water is stored and piped to home taps
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one body of water all the way from rain to tap, stage by stage, and watch what makes it safe to drink.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain the water supply in stages: rain collected in a reservoir, raw water drawn to the treatment works, treatment cleaning stage by stage, cleaned water stored and piped to home taps
Name what happens at each stage and why the cleanliness bar climbs only during treatment
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to tell the whole journey of the water in the right order.

slides.heading: The water at the tap is clean - was it clean when the rain was collected?
bullets: Rain looks clean as it falls, and reservoir water looks clear in photographs
Did collecting the water make it safe to drink, or is there more of the journey still to come?
slides.notes: Ask the class: when water looks clear, does that mean it is safe to drink straight away? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation follows the water through every stage.

slides.heading: Collected water is raw water - treatment makes it tap water
bullets: Water collected in a reservoir is raw water: it still carries dirt and germs, and moving it to the treatment works does not clean it
Treatment stages remove dirt and germs step by step, and only the cleaned water is stored and piped to home taps
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: collection starts the journey, treatment does the cleaning - the stages in between are what make tap water safe.

slides.heading: Stage 1: rain is collected in a reservoir
bullets: Rain falls on the catchment and is collected in a reservoir, where it is stored as raw water
This water is not yet safe to drink - it still carries dirt and germs, and the cleanliness bar is low
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the rain, the reservoir and the low cleanliness bar: this is the start of the supply chain, not the end.

slides.heading: Stage 2: raw water is drawn to the treatment works
bullets: Pipes draw the raw water out of the reservoir and carry it to the treatment works
Moving the water does not clean it - the cleanliness bar barely moves on the journey
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the blob of water along the pipe: it arrives at the treatment works still raw, still carrying dirt and germs.

slides.heading: Stage 3: treatment cleans the water, stage by stage
bullets: At the treatment works the water passes through stages one at a time: dirt settles and sinks, then germs are trapped and removed
The cleanliness bar climbs at every treatment stage - 70 to 140 to 210 to 280 - as dirt and germs are removed
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and pause at each tank: settling removes dirt, filtering traps germs, and the bar climbs only when a stage removes something.

slides.heading: Stage 4: clean water is stored and piped to home taps
bullets: Only after treatment is the cleaned water stored and piped to home taps, and the cleanliness bar is full
The wrong-turn shortcut - drinking the water straight from the reservoir - is played out and corrected: treatment comes first
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and contrast the two routes: the shortcut skips every cleaning stage, the real route treats first, then stores and pipes the water home.

slides.heading: Worked example: following one body of water from rain to tap
bullets: Start: rain is collected in a reservoir and stored as raw water, not yet safe to drink
Finish: clean tap water at home - reached only after the water is drawn to the treatment works and cleaned stage by stage, then stored and piped home
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Stage 1, rain collected in a reservoir. Stage 2, raw water drawn to the treatment works. Stage 3, treatment cleans the water stage by stage. Stage 4, cleaned water stored and piped to home taps. At each stage ask: what happens to the water here, and does the bar climb?

slides.heading: Your turn: run the stages in order
bullets: In pairs: starting from rain falling on the catchment, name each stage in order and say what happens to the water and to the cleanliness bar at that stage
Then swap and check: did your partner send the water through treatment before the tap, or jump straight from the reservoir to drinking?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for all four stages in order, then take two pairs answers: reservoir, treatment works, cleaned and stored, home taps.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says collected water is already safe to drink
Name the treatment stages the water still has to pass through to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers keep raw water and tap water apart and run the stages in order.
